 KATSEYE's Yoonchae brings K-beauty roots to Dr.Jart+'s North America campaign
 KATSEYE's Yoonchae fronts Dr.Jart+'s North America BB cream campaign, combining Korean beauty heritage with candid backstage storytelling.
 Zoe Park 
 05 Nov 2026 
 • 3 min read 
 ✦

 ↓ 
 KATSEYE's Yoonchae is taking her Korean beauty routine into a new spotlight. For a group whose appeal crosses languages and national borders, the choice of a Korean member to front a Korean skincare label in North America carries a recognizable cultural connection. This time, the product at the center is a BB cream, not a new single or dance challenge.
 Dr.Jart+ named Yoonchae Jeung its first-ever North America brand ambassador on October 30. The 18-year-old performer fronts a digital-first push for the reformulated Premium BB Cream SPF 30, using behind-the-scenes moments, previously unseen user-generated content and a documentary-style video rather than just a conventional beauty portrait.

 Why Yoonchae's Korean background matters 
 How the BB cream fits the backstage story 
 What the partnership says about K-pop beauty marketing 
 Why Yoonchae's Korean background matters
 KATSEYE is a globally oriented pop group whose members bring different backgrounds and personal styles to the same stage. That gives Yoonchae a natural role in a beauty story that moves between Seoul and Los Angeles. In a Cosmopolitan interview tied to the campaign, she described growing up with Korean beauty practices and discovering new makeup looks after moving to LA.
 Dr.Jart+ was founded in Seoul in 2005. Its global brand lead Ye Jin Kim explained the company's approach in the announcement: “Music, especially K-pop, has always been an important part of how Dr.Jart+ shows up in culture.” The brand previously partnered with ENHYPEN, so Yoonchae's appointment builds on an existing music connection. The first-ever claim refers specifically to its North America ambassador position, not to its first partnership with a Korean artist.
 For fans who know Yoonchae primarily through performances and music videos, the appeal of backstage beauty content is that it shifts the focus from the finished stage look to the preparation around it. The company has outlined that format, although it has not released verified audience-response figures for this particular campaign.
 How the BB cream fits the backstage story
 Premium BB Cream SPF 30 is a skincare-and-makeup hybrid. Dr.Jart+ says the reformulated product contains 2% niacinamide and glycerin, is sold in eight shades and costs US$49 for 40ml. These are brand-provided product specifications, not independent effectiveness findings.
 The creative concept draws on the busy schedule of a performer. A BB cream that combines coverage and skincare is presented as part of a quick routine, while candid clips and documentary-style footage give viewers more context than a static endorsement. Yoonchae told the brand that she values a simple routine that helps her feel confident even when her schedule is full.
 That makes the campaign more specific than a celebrity simply holding a product. The product's all-in-one positioning is tied to the everyday work behind a polished pop performance, giving the beauty message a role within the artist's story.
 What the partnership says about K-pop beauty marketing
 The collaboration also sits alongside other KATSEYE brand work, including Gap's denim campaign. That fashion collaboration leaned into choreography and group identity, while Dr.Jart+ narrows the lens to one member and her personal skincare habits. The contrast shows how a global group's cultural reach can support both ensemble storytelling and individual endorsements.
 For Dr.Jart+, the North America designation makes the geographic ambition explicit. A Seoul-born artist with an international fan base is introducing a Korean beauty product to a market where her group already has visibility. The campaign's success cannot yet be assessed from the announcement alone: Dr.Jart+ has not disclosed its ambassador fee, campaign reach, sales lift or conversion results.
 The more interesting marketing choice is the storytelling format. By pairing Yoonchae's personal routine with a product designed to simplify a beauty routine, Dr.Jart+ is giving fans a reason to watch beyond the celebrity name. Whether that attention turns into sustained product demand remains an open question.
